speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your baby's condition, could you please describe exactly when these episodes of stridor and wheezing tend to occur? For instance, do they happen during feeding, crying, or when the infant is in a specific position?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice if the stridor improves when the infant's neck is extended or when he is lying on his back? Have you observed any cyanosis or apnea during these episodes, and has he failed to thrive or had difficulty gaining weight?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of positional stridor relieved by neck extension and exacerbated by crying or feeding is highly suggestive of vascular compression of the airway. I will request imaging to confirm the anatomical cause before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the neck and chest

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI was normal, we must consider other causes of vascular compression or airway anomalies that might not be as clearly defined on standard imaging. REQUEST TEST: Chest CT angiography

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest CT angiography confirms the presence of a double aortic arch with compression of the trachea and esophagus.
